title: Erdős Problem #596: Graph Coloring Dichotomy for Forbidden Subgraphs
description: For which pairs (G₁, G₂) is it true that for every n there exists a G₁-free graph whose n-colorings contain monochromatic G₂, yet every G₁-free graph admits a countable coloring avoiding monochromatic G₂? OPEN.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #596 from [Er87] asks for a characterization of graph pairs (G₁, G₂) satisfying a finite/countable Ramsey-type dichotomy. Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured no such pairs exist, but Nešetřil-Rödl and Erdős-Hajnal showed that (C₄, C₆) is a valid pair. The related Problem #595 asks specifically about (K₄, K₃). The structural Ramsey theory context here traces back to the Nešetřil-Rödl theorem of the 1970s, which proved that for any graph H there exist graphs with arbitrarily high chromatic number containing no odd cycle shorter than any fixed length. Erdős and Hajnal's result that C₄-free graphs decompose into countably many trees (a consequence of their work on sparse graphs) provided the key tool for the countable coloring half of the (C₄, C₆) dichotomy.
overview.problemStatement: For which pairs (G₁, G₂) is it true that (1) for every n, there exists a G₁-free graph H such that every n-coloring of H's edges contains a monochromatic G₂, and (2) every G₁-free graph H admits a countable edge coloring with no monochromatic G₂? OPEN.
overview.text: For which pairs (G₁, G₂) is it true that for every n there exists a G₁-free graph whose n-colorings contain monochromatic G₂, yet every G₁-free graph admits a countable coloring avoiding monochromatic G₂? OPEN.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines GraphProperty, FiniteRamseyProperty, CountableColoringProperty, and HasDichotomy. The known pair (C₄, C₆) is proved to satisfy the dichotomy from axioms of Nešetřil-Rödl and Erdős-Hajnal. The main problem asks for a complete characterization.
keyInsights: The dichotomy combines a finite Ramsey property with a countable coloring property
Erdős-Hajnal originally conjectured no pairs exist, but (C₄, C₆) is a counterexample
C₄-free graphs are countable unions of trees (Erdős-Hajnal)
The pair (K₄, K₃) is an important open case (Problem #595)
Connected to structural Ramsey theory and graph decomposition

sections.title: Part I: Graph Coloring Dichotomy
sections.summary: Defines GraphProperty, FiniteRamseyProperty, CountableColoringProperty, and HasDichotomy.
sections.mathContext: FiniteRamseyProperty$(G_1, G_2)$: $\forall n, \exists H$ $G_1$-free such that every $n$-coloring of $E(H)$ has monochromatic $G_2$. CountableColoringProperty: every $G_1$-free $H$ admits $c : E(H) \to \mathbb{N}$ with no monochromatic $G_2$.

sections.title: Part II: Known Examples
sections.summary: Defines IsC4Free, ContainsC6. Axioms: nesetril_rodl_c4_c6 (Ramsey for C₄-free/C₆), erdos_hajnal_c4_trees (C₄-free → countable decomposition).
sections.mathContext: Nešetřil-Rödl: $\forall n, \exists$ $C_4$-free $H$ with every $n$-coloring containing monochromatic $C_6$. Erdős-Hajnal: $C_4$-free graphs decompose into countably many forests.

sections.title: Part III: The Known Dichotomy Pair
sections.summary: Theorem c4_c6_dichotomy: (C₄, C₆) has the dichotomy property.
sections.mathContext: $(C_4, C_6)$ satisfies both properties simultaneously — initially thought impossible by Erdős-Hajnal.

sections.title: Part IV: The Main Conjecture
sections.summary: Defines ErdosProblem596: existence of a structural characterization. Axiom erdos_596.
sections.mathContext: The problem asks for a classification: which $(G_1, G_2)$ satisfy HasDichotomy? Is there a structural characterization?

sections.title: Part V: Related Problem (K₄, K₃)
sections.summary: Defines IsK4Free, ContainsK3. Axiom erdos_595_k4_k3 for the (K₄, K₃) case.
sections.mathContext: Problem #595: Does $(K_4, K_3)$ satisfy the dichotomy? Can $K_4$-free graphs always avoid monochromatic triangles with countably many colors?

sections.title: Part VI: Properties
sections.summary: Theorem dichotomy_pairs_exist: at least one dichotomy pair exists.

sections.title: Part VII: Summary
sections.summary: erdos_596_summary: conjunction of dichotomy and existence results. Problem remains OPEN.
sections.mathContext: Packages known results: $(C_4, C_6)$ has dichotomy and dichotomy pairs exist. Classification for all pairs remains open.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #596 asks for a characterization of graph pairs (G₁, G₂) satisfying a finite/countable Ramsey dichotomy. The pair (C₄, C₆) is a known example, but the general characterization remains open.
conclusion.implications: Resolution would clarify the structural Ramsey theory of forbidden subgraph classes and their decomposition into countably many simple pieces.
openQuestions: Which pairs (G₁, G₂) satisfy the dichotomy?
Is there a finite characterization of all dichotomy pairs?
What structural properties of G₁-free graphs determine the dichotomy?
